questions.question: 15 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹7,800 and 14 chairs and 6 tables cost ₹9,200. What is the cost of 17 chairs and 18 tables?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the first **cost** equation to: 5 **chairs** + 1 **table** = ₹2,600.

Multiply this by 6 to match **tables** in the second case: 30 **chairs** + 6 **tables** = ₹15,600.

Difference with second equation: (30 − 14) **chairs** = ₹15,600 − ₹9,200 ⇒ 16 **chairs** = ₹6,400.

Cost of 1 **chair** = ₹400 and cost of 1 **table** = 2,600 − (5 × 400) = ₹600.

Required **total cost** = 17 × 400 + 18 × 600 = 6,800 + 10,800 = ₹17,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

15 **chairs** (C) + 3 **tables** (T) = ₹7,800

14 **chairs** (C) + 6 **tables** (T) = ₹9,200

**Formula Used:**

**Linear Equation** solving using the **elimination method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1836d5b016f522760c829376d675f5c10507661dfebf518b68f246358582f6c4.png] 

⇒ Let **chair** cost be C and **table** cost be T.

⇒ 15C + 3T = 7,800 ⇒ 5C + T = 2,600 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ 14C + 6T = 9,200 ⇒ 7C + 3T = 4,600 ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 3: 15C + 3T = 7,800

⇒ Subtract Equation 2 from (Equation 1 × 3): (15C + 3T) − (7C + 3T) = 7,800 − 4,600

⇒ 8C = 3,200 ⇒ C = 400

⇒ Substitute C in Eq 1: 5(400) + T = 2,600 ⇒ T = 2,600 − 2,000 = 600

⇒ Cost of 17 **chairs** and 18 **tables** = 17 × 400 + 18 × 600

⇒ 6,800 + 10,800 = 17,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Equations of the form ax + by = c represent a straight line. Solving two such equations finds the intersection point (x, y).

Elimination Method

A process of eliminating one variable by making its coefficients equal in both equations through multiplication, then adding or subtracting.

Substitution Method

Expressing one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substituting it into the second equation to solve for one variable first.

questions.question: An award made by a Lok Adalat has the same status as a ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Court decree**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An award made by a Lok Adalat is considered to have the same legal status as a **decree of a Civil Court.**
 
• It is deemed final and binding on all parties involved, and no appeal lies against it in any court of law.
 
• The Lok Adalat system works under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, promoting alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
• It resolves disputes through conciliation and compromise, offering an accessible and cost-effective mechanism for justice.
 
• Once a dispute is settled by Lok Adalat, it is enforceable as a Civil Court decree under Section 21 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat**

 
 
• Lok Adalat translates to "People's Court" and is an integral part of the Indian judicial system.
 
• It is an alternative dispute resolution forum aimed at reducing the burden on regular courts.
 
• It is free of cost and does not require payment of court fees by the disputing parties.
 
• Lok Adalats are organized at various levels, including state, district, and taluk levels.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**
 
 
• This Act provides the statutory basis for the establishment of Lok Adalats in India.
 
• The Act aims to provide free and competent legal services to weaker sections of society.
 
• It promotes the resolution of disputes amicably and ensures that justice is accessible to all.
 
 
 
• **Types of Cases Handled by Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Cases related to civil disputes, including matrimonial and property disputes.
 
• Compoundable criminal cases and cases under the Motor Vehicles Act.
 
• Disputes related to bank recovery, labor matters, and public utility services.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Ensures speedy justice and reduces the backlog of cases in regular courts.
 
• It is a cost-effective and informal forum for dispute resolution.
 
• Encourages amicable settlement through mutual consent and eliminates procedural complexities.

questions.question: Who were the 'Rajukas' during the Mauryan period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Provincial officials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Rajukas' during the Mauryan period were **provincial officials responsible for administration and justice in their designated regions**.
 
• They were appointed by the central authority and were often tasked with overseeing matters of governance, including **maintaining law and order**.
 
• Rajukas played a pivotal role in implementing the policies and edicts of Emperor Ashoka, especially concerning **Dhamma or moral governance**.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, and Rajukas formed part of the administrative machinery that ensured the smooth functioning of provincial governance.
 
• Inscriptions like Ashoka's edicts mention Rajukas as being entrusted with both **administrative duties and judicial responsibilities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centralized Administration in Mauryan Empire:**

 
 
• The Mauryan Empire, established by Chandragupta Maurya, was known for its **efficient and centralized administrative structure**.
 
• Provinces were governed by officials like Rajukas and were directly accountable to the Emperor.
 
 
 
• **Dhamma of Ashoka:**
 
 
• Emperor Ashoka's policy of Dhamma emphasized **ethical conduct, non-violence, and social welfare**.
 
• Rajukas were instrumental in promoting Dhamma and ensuring its implementation across the empire.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The Mauryan administrative structure included officials like **Amatyas (ministers), Rajukas (provincial officials), and Yuktas (subordinate officers)**.
 
• This hierarchy ensured the smooth functioning of governance from the central authority down to local levels.
 
 
 
• **Edicts of Ashoka:**
 
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions, such as the Rock and Pillar Edicts, provide valuable insights into the role of Rajukas in governance and justice.
 
• These edicts also highlight the emperor's emphasis on **compassionate and moral administration**.

In lipid biochemistry, why do unsaturated fatty acids tend to be liquid at room temperature?

options.text: They form ionic bonds that prevent solidification.
The cis-double bonds introduce kinks, reducing van der Waals interactions.
Their double bonds increase molecular symmetry leading to less crystal packing.
They have lower molecular weights than saturated fatty acids.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The cis-double bonds introduce kinks, reducing van der Waals interactions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids have **cis-double bonds** that introduce kinks in their hydrocarbon chains.
 
• These kinks prevent tight packing of the fatty acid molecules, thereby **reducing van der Waals interactions**.
 
• As a result, unsaturated fatty acids have **lower melting points** compared to saturated fatty acids, making them liquid at room temperature.
 
• The inability to tightly pack molecules leads to a more **fluid structure**, which is characteristic of oils derived from unsaturated fatty acids.
 
• The degree of unsaturation (number of double bonds) further influences the extent of fluidity in these molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Van der Waals interactions:**

 
 
• These are weak forces of attraction between molecules due to temporary dipoles.
 
• In saturated fatty acids, tight packing results in stronger van der Waals forces, contributing to solid state at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Cis and trans configurations:**
 
 
• Cis-double bonds introduce bends or kinks in the fatty acid chains, while trans-double bonds allow linear structures.
 
• Trans fats behave more like saturated fats and are often solid at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Saturated vs Unsaturated Fatty Acids:**
 
 
• Saturated fatty acids lack double bonds, allowing tighter molecular packing.
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids contain one or more double bonds, which disrupt packing and increase fluidity.
 
 
 
• **Role in cell membranes:**
 
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids contribute to membrane fluidity, essential for cellular functions.
 
• Phospholipids with unsaturated fatty acid tails are a key component of biological membranes.
 
 
 
• **Melting points of fatty acids:**
 
 
• Saturated fatty acids like stearic acid have higher melting points.
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids like oleic acid are liquid at room temperature due to disrupted packing.

questions.question: Which group gained increased importance in the post-Gupta society due to land grants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the post-Gupta period, the practice of granting land to Brahmins increased substantially, enhancing their social and economic importance.
 
• Land grants to Brahmins were often tax-free and hereditary, leading to their domination in rural areas and control over village resources.
 
• Brahmins were seen as custodians of religious knowledge and traditions, which justified their elevated status in society.
 
• This practice strengthened the Brahminical social order and contributed to the spread of Hindu religion and culture during this period.
 
• The land grants were typically accompanied by the responsibility of maintaining temples and performing rituals, further solidifying Brahmins' central role in religious and social life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Land Grants:**

 
 
• Land grants, known as "Agrahara," were often given to Brahmins as a mark of respect and recognition of their religious status.
 
• These grants exempted the recipient from paying taxes and often included rights over the produce and labor of the land.
 
 
 
• **Brahminical Social Order:**
 
 
• The Brahmins were at the top of the Varna system, which structured society into hierarchical groups.
 
• This period saw the consolidation of the caste system, with Brahmins maintaining dominance in religious, educational, and administrative spheres.
 
 
 
• **Post-Gupta Period:**
 
 
• The post-Gupta era (6th-12th century CE) witnessed feudal elements in Indian society, with land grants becoming a key feature of governance.
 
• This period marked the decline of central authority and the rise of regional powers, making land ownership a crucial aspect of political control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Rural Society:**
 
 
• Land grants led to the emergence of Brahmins as powerful intermediaries between the rulers and the peasants.
 
• They played a significant role in managing village resources, resolving disputes, and maintaining social order.

questions.question: How does the writ jurisdiction of the High Courts differ from that of the Supreme Court?

options.text: High Courts require prior approval from the Supreme Court before issuing writs.
High Courts can issue writs only against state governments, not the Centre.
High Courts can issue writs only in appellate cases, not in original jurisdiction.
High Courts can issue writs for purposes beyond Fundamental Rights, unlike the Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Courts can issue writs for purposes beyond Fundamental Rights, unlike the Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **High Courts have broader writ jurisdiction** as they can issue writs not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for other legal rights.
 
• The Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction under **Article 32** of the Constitution is restricted to the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• High Courts derive their writ jurisdiction from **Article 226**, which explicitly allows them to issue writs for any other purpose besides Fundamental Rights.
 
• This expanded scope enables High Courts to address issues such as administrative orders, statutory duties, and violations of legal rights, providing greater flexibility.
 
• Both courts can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writ Jurisdiction Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** Used to ensure a person's release from unlawful detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** Directs public officials or bodies to perform their duties.
 
• **Prohibition:** Prevents lower courts from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** Allows higher courts to quash orders of lower courts if they acted beyond their jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** Questions the legal authority of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Article 32 vs Article 226:**
 
 
• **Article 32:** Grants the Supreme Court exclusive powers to issue writs for Fundamental Rights enforcement.
 
• **Article 226:** Provides High Courts with expanded writ jurisdiction for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
• Article 226 is considered broader in scope than Article 32.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Enshrined under Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• Include rights such as equality, freedom of speech, protection against discrimination, and right to constitutional remedies.
 
• Writs are a mechanism to enforce these rights.
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights:**
 
 
• These are rights granted by statutes or laws, such as property rights, contract rights, etc.
 
• High Courts can issue writs for their enforcement under Article 226.

questions.question: A man takes 13 hours to swim 91 km downstream. He swims 39 km upstream in the same time. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed (D) = 91 ÷ 13 = 7 km/hr

Upstream speed (U) = 39 ÷ 13 = 3 km/hr

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (7 + 3) ÷ 2 = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dadcd20c213dd68eb1a2c6b89a3a1bd1527d6ac333cf327cf8e7461174c1b18e.png] 

**Given:**

Downstream Distance = 91 km, Upstream Distance = 39 km, Time = 13 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of boat (u) = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed (v + s) = 91 ÷ 13 = 7 km/hr

⇒ Upstream speed (v − s) = 39 ÷ 13 = 3 km/hr

⇒ Adding both equations: 2v = 7 + 3

⇒ 2v = 10

⇒ v = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The speed of the current or stream is calculated as (Downstream speed − Upstream speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed in Still Water

If a boat travels the same distance downstream and upstream, the average speed in still water is the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream. Upstream speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream.</p

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,000 at 5.75% per annum rate of interest for the period from 15 February 2023 to 29 April 2023.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given period into **standard day fractions**: 73 days is exactly 1/5 of a year (73 × 5 = 365).

Net Rate for the period = 5.75% ÷ 5 = 1.15%.

Simple Interest = 1.15% of ₹2,000 = 1.15 × 20 = ₹23.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹2,000**

Rate (R) = **5.75% per annum**

Time Period = **15 February 2023 to 29 April 2023**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3a8581ab2208ab47d08865ec8c261a60c0c295e39cb663e86c28a0b497a3189.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in **February** (Non-leap year) = 28 − 15 = **13 days**

⇒ Number of days in **March** = **31 days**

⇒ Number of days in **April** = **29 days**

⇒ Total days = 13 + 31 + 29 = **73 days**

⇒ Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = **1/5 years**

⇒ SI = (2000 × 5.75 × 1/5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (400 × 5.75) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 4 × 5.75

⇒ SI = **₹23**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time Calculation Rule

While calculating the number of days, the day on which money is **deposited** is usually excluded and the day on which money is **withdrawn** is included.

Leap Year Consideration

If the period includes **29 February**, the total days in the year are taken as **366** instead of 365.

Amount Formula

The total **Amount (A)** to be paid at the end of the term is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: **A = P + SI**.

questions.question: A water tank can be filled in 19 minutes by using 39 pipes of the same capacity . In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 23 pipes of the same capacity as above?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Apply the **Inverse Proportion** rule: **M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂**

Where **M** is the number of **pipes** and **T** is the **time** taken.

39 × 19 = 23 × T₂

T₂ = 741 ÷ 23 ≈ 32.22

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (P₁) = **39 pipes**

Initial time taken (T₁) = **19 minutes**

Final number of pipes (P₂) = **23 pipes**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Pipes × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Capacity of Tank = 39 × 19 = **741 units**

⇒ Required Time (T₂) = Total Capacity ÷ Number of Pipes

⇒ T₂ = 741 ÷ 23

⇒ T₂ = 32.21739...

⇒ T₂ ≈ **32.22 minutes** (rounded off to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Work

When the **efficiency** of each unit is constant, the time required is **inversely proportional** to the number of units (pipes/men). If pipes decrease, time increases.

Chain Rule Formula

The general relation is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is power, D/H is time, and W is work.</p

questions.question: Convectional rainfall is common in which part of India during the pre-monsoon period?

• This region experiences high temperatures during the pre-monsoon months (March to May), which leads to the formation of cumulus clouds and subsequent rainfall.
 
• The rainfall is often accompanied by thunderstorms and is locally known as **"Nor'westers" or "Kal Baisakhi"** in eastern India.

• The plateau experiences extreme weather conditions, including hot summers and convectional rains during pre-monsoon periods.

• They are common in eastern India, especially in West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha, during the pre-monsoon season.
 
• The term "Kal Baisakhi" translates to "Calamity of Baisakh" (a month in the Hindu calendar).
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**

• The accompanying thunderstorms can sometimes damage standing crops due to hail or strong winds.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 17 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 16 km/hr. A man rows to a place at a distance of 26.4 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time (in hours) taken by him.

**Downstream Speed** (D) = 17 + 16 = 33 km/hr

**Upstream Speed** (U) = 17 − 16 = 1 km/hr

**Total Time** = (Distance ÷ D) + (Distance ÷ U)

**Total Time** = (26.4 ÷ 33) + (26.4 ÷ 1) = 0.8 + 26.4 = 27.2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 27.2 hours.**

**Speed of stream** (v) = 16 km/hr

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = u + v

Upstream Speed = u − v

⇒ Downstream Speed = 17 + 16 = 33 km/hr

⇒ Upstream Speed = 17 − 16 = 1 km/hr

⇒ Time taken downstream (t₁) = 26.4 ÷ 33 = 0.8 hours

⇒ Time taken upstream (t₂) = 26.4 ÷ 1 = 26.4 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ = 0.8 + 26.4 = 27.2 hours

Downstream Speed

When the boat moves in the direction of the stream, its effective speed is the sum of the boat speed and stream speed (u + v).

Upstream Speed

When the boat moves against the direction of the stream, its effective speed is the difference between the boat speed and stream speed (u − v).

Average Speed for Round Trip

The average speed for a boat going to a point and returning is given by: Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Speed of Boat in Still Water.</p

questions.question: Find the effective price percentage of the marked price after three consecutive discounts of 8%, 17% and 17%. (Rounded up to two decimal places.)

questions.question:
What is the median of the following data?

15, 70, 34, 37, 25, 36, 74, 36, 54, 78, 33
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given **11 observations** in ascending order:

15, 25, 33, 34, 36, **36**, 37, 54, 70, 74, 78

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is **odd**, the median is the middle-most term:

Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **36**

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given data:** 15, 70, 34, 37, 25, 36, 74, 36, 54, 78, 33

**Total number of observations (N):** 11

**Formula:**

When N is odd, Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation (after sorting in ascending order).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fea7786b15ca10ff3bd60f4e953318df16fb4822fc2c26f567b42f6dbf7bca10.png] 

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Arrange the given data in ascending order:

⇒ 15, 25, 33, 34, 36, 36, 37, 54, 70, 74, 78

Step 2: Count the total number of observations (N):

⇒ N = 11 (which is an odd number)

Step 3: Apply the median formula for odd N:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th observation

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th observation

⇒ Median = 6th observation

Step 4: Identify the 6th observation from the sorted list:

⇒ 6th observation = 36

**Why other options are incorrect:**

• **Option (1) 36.5:** This would be the median if the number of observations was even and the two middle terms averaged to 36.5. Since N is odd (11), the median must be an actual term from the dataset.

• **Option (3) 35.5:** This is not the middle value of the sorted dataset.

• **Option (4) 37:** This is the 7th term in the sorted dataset, not the middle (6th) term.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Observations

If the number of observations (N) is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th and ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th terms after sorting.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Effect of Outliers on Median

Unlike the mean, the median is highly robust and is not affected by extreme values (outliers) in the dataset.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) is INCORRECT?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are used in a wide range of electronic devices, including both **desktop computers and portable devices** like smartphones, laptops, and tablets.

• Advancements in PCB technology, such as flexible and rigid-flex PCBs, have enabled their integration into portable and wearable devices.

questions.question: Under whose administration was the practice of Sati officially abolished in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck was the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• The practice of Sati, where widows were forced to self-immolate on their husband’s funeral pyre, was officially abolished during his administration in **1829**.
 
• The abolition was enforced through the Bengal Sati Regulation, **Regulation XVII of 1829**, which declared Sati as illegal and punishable by law.
 
• Bentinck took this reform initiative due to advocacy by social reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who strongly opposed the practice.
 
• The regulation applied initially to Bengal Presidency and was later extended to other parts of British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**

 
 
• A prominent social reformer who played a key role in advocating for the abolition of Sati.
 
• He argued that Sati had no religious sanction and was opposed to the core teachings of Hindu scriptures.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Modern India" for his reformist efforts.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829:**
 
 
• It was enacted on December 4, 1829, by Lord William Bentinck.
 
• The regulation declared the practice of Sati as illegal, punishable by the courts, and equivalent to culpable homicide.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Sati Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition marked a significant step in social reform during British rule in India.
 
• It helped pave the way for future reforms concerning women’s rights and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck's Legacy:**
 
 
• Besides abolishing Sati, Bentinck introduced other reforms such as the promotion of Western education and suppression of Thuggee.
 
• He is remembered for his progressive approach toward governance and reform in India.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 44?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by **44** if it is divisible by both **4** and **11**.

Check **Divisibility by 4**: Last two digits must be divisible by 4. Only **3344** (44 ÷ 4 = 11) satisfies this.

Check **Divisibility by 11** for 3344: (3 + 4) − (3 + 4) = 0. Since the difference is 0, it is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3344.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 3379, 3344, 3550, 2967.

**Condition:** Number must be divisible by 44 (i.e., 4 × 11).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45af1643594905f7e38d19f3852777979abe2ea61348e71e7358f6677da8880c.png] 

⇒ Divisibility by 4: Last two digits of **3344** are **44**. 44 ÷ 4 = 11 (Divisible).

⇒ Divisibility by 11: Sum of odd place digits = 3 + 4 = 7; Sum of even place digits = 3 + 4 = 7.

⇒ Difference = 7 − 7 = 0. Since result is 0, it is divisible by 11.

⇒ Other options: 3379 (odd), 3550 (50 not div by 4), 2967 (odd) fail the test.

**∴ The correct answer is 3344.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its **last two digits** are divisible by 4 or if the last two digits are 00.

Divisibility Rule of 11

The **difference** between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number **N**, check divisibility by its **co-prime factors** (e.g., for 12, check 3 and 4).</p

questions.question: The Northern Plains of India have been primarily formed by which of the following processes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deposition of alluvium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plains of India were formed due to the **deposition of alluvial soil brought by the rivers** originating from the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The plains are composed of layers of **fine silt, sand, and clay** deposited over millions of years.
 
• The three major Himalayan rivers—**the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus**—along with their tributaries, played a crucial role in shaping these fertile plains.
 
• This region is known for its **fertile soil**, making it one of the most agriculturally productive areas in India.
 
• The Northern Plains are categorized into three sections—**the Bhabar, the Terai, and the Alluvial Plains** (Khadar and Bangar).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvium:**

 
 
• Alluvium refers to the **fine-grained fertile soil** deposited by rivers over time.
 
• This type of soil is rich in minerals and nutrients, making it suitable for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• The rivers originating from the Himalayas, such as the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus, are **perennial**, meaning they flow throughout the year.
 
• These rivers are fed by **glacial melt** and monsoon rains.
 
 
 
• **Bhabar and Terai:**
 
 
• **Bhabar:** A narrow belt of coarse gravel and pebbles found at the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• **Terai:** A marshy and swampy region south of the Bhabar, characterized by dense vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Khadar and Bangar:**
 
 
• **Khadar:** The newer, fertile alluvial soil found in the river's floodplains.
 
• **Bangar:** The older alluvial soil found further away from the riverbanks, less fertile than Khadar.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Significance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plains are often referred to as the "Granary of India" due to their high agricultural output.
 
• Main crops grown in the region include wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

questions.question: If the third proportional of 40 and Z is 10, then what is the positive value of Z?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two numbers **40** and **Z**, if the **third proportional** is **10**, then **Z² = 40 × 10**.

⇒ **Z² = 400**

⇒ **Z = √400 = 20**

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number (a) = **40**, Second number (b) = **Z**, Third proportional (c) = **10**.

**Formula Used:** If **a, b, c** are in **continued proportion**, then **a/b = b/c**, which means **b² = ac**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81d71712dd2ec7d6f555840bb08cf6474dbce7c213af620cfa6cfe32457074c6.png] 

⇒ 40 : Z :: Z : 10

⇒ 40 / Z = Z / 10

⇒ Z × Z = 40 × 10

⇒ Z² = 400

⇒ Z = √400

⇒ Z = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a, b, c, d** are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then the fourth proportional **d** is **(b × c) / a**.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of **a:b** and **c:d** is **(ac):(bd)**, obtained by multiplying corresponding terms.</p

questions.question: What does PCB stand for in electronics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Printed Circuit Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Printed Circuit Board (PCB)** is a non-conductive board that holds and connects electronic components using conductive pathways, pads, and tracks etched from copper sheets.
 
• PCBs are used in almost all electronic devices, including mobile phones, computers, televisions, and industrial equipment.
 
• They are essential for simplifying and streamlining the manufacturing and assembly process of electronic circuits.
 
• PCBs can be single-layered, double-layered, or multi-layered, depending on the complexity of the circuit and application.
 
• PCBs replaced traditional wire-based circuits, making devices more compact, efficient, and reliable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Substrate:** The base material, usually fiberglass, providing the board's rigidity.
 
• **Copper Layer:** Conductive layer used for electrical connections.
 
• **Solder Mask:** Protective layer applied over the copper to prevent short circuits.
 
• **Silkscreen:** Layer for labeling components and providing assembly guidance.
 
 
 
• **Types of PCBs:**
 
 
• **Single-Sided PCBs:** Copper traces are present only on one side of the board.
 
• **Double-Sided PCBs:** Copper traces exist on both sides, interconnected by vias.
 
• **Multi-Layered PCBs:** Composed of multiple layers of copper and insulating material.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of PCBs:**
 
 
• Compact and lightweight design, leading to smaller electronic devices.
 
• Increased reliability due to reduced wiring complexity and consistent manufacturing.
 
• Cost-effective in mass production.
 
 
 
• **Applications of PCBs:**
 
 
• Consumer electronics like smartphones, laptops, and televisions.
 
• Automotive systems, including sensors and control modules.
 
• Medical devices such as pacemakers and imaging systems.
 
• Industrial equipment used in manufacturing and robotics.

questions.question: If 3 cotA = 2, then find the value of sqrt{frac{3(operatorname{cosec}² A - 1)}{(sec² A - 1)}}

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 3 **cotA** = 2 ⇒ **cotA** = 2/3.

The expression simplifies using **trigonometric identities**: **cosec²A − 1** = **cot²A** and **sec²A − 1** = **tan²A**.

Value = √[3 × **cot²A** / **tan²A**] = √[3 × **cot⁴A**] = **cot²A** × √3.

Value = (2/3)² × √3 = (4/9) × √3 = 4√3/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4√3/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 **cotA** = 2

**Formula Used:** 1 + **cot²A** = **cosec²A**; 1 + **tan²A** = **sec²A**; **tanA** = 1/**cotA**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8daeee01db7df3fa6fb0a4abb0ee733d02e605c03725c494ddb1159a8cd93664.png] 

⇒ **cotA** = 2/3

⇒ **cosec²A − 1** = **cot²A** = (2/3)² = 4/9

⇒ **sec²A − 1** = **tan²A** = (3/2)² = 9/4

⇒ Expression = √[3 × (4/9) / (9/4)]

⇒ Expression = √[3 × (4/9) × (4/9)]

⇒ Expression = (4/9) × √3 = 4√3/9

**∴ The correct answer is 4√3/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; sec²θ − tan²θ = 1; cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

tanθ = 1/cotθ; sinθ = 1/cosecθ; cosθ = 1/secθ.</p

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Sahkar' taxi service, launched by the Indian government in March 2025?

options.text: To empower drivers through a cooperative, profit-sharing model
To establish a government-owned ride-hailing monopoly
To provide free taxi services to senior citizens
To replace all existing private taxi services in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To empower drivers through a cooperative, profit-sharing model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Sahkar' taxi service was launched by the Indian government in March 2025 to **empower drivers through a cooperative model**, ensuring equitable profit-sharing.
 
• It aims to provide a sustainable livelihood for drivers by eliminating intermediary exploitation and promoting transparency in the industry.
 
• The service functions as a driver-owned cooperative, where profits are distributed among the members, fostering social and financial inclusion.
 
• This initiative aligns with the government's agenda of promoting cooperative enterprises as a way to boost employment and self-reliance.
 
• The Sahkar taxi service is expected to encourage fair practices and improve working conditions for drivers in India, especially in urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cooperative Model:**

 
 
• A cooperative is a member-owned organization that operates for the benefit of its members rather than external shareholders.
 
• It is based on principles of voluntary participation, democratic governance, and equitable profit-sharing.
 
• Cooperatives often focus on improving livelihoods and promoting social equity.
 
 
 
• **Indian Government Initiatives in Cooperative Sector:**
 
 
• The government has been actively promoting cooperatives through schemes like the **National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)**.
 
• It has introduced legislative reforms to strengthen cooperative societies and improve their governance.
 
 
 
• **Employment Generation through Cooperatives:**

questions.question:
The volume of a right circular cylinder is 4851 cm³ and its curved surface area is 462 cm². If this cylinder is generated by rotating a rectangle about its length by 360°, what will be the perimeter (in cm) of this rectangle?

Use pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volume (V)** to **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** gives radius directly: V / CSA = (πr²h) / (2πrh) = r / 2.

4851 / 462 = r / 2 ⇒ 10.5 = r / 2 ⇒ **r = 21 cm**.

Using CSA: 2 × (22/7) × 21 × h = 462 ⇒ 132 × h = 462 ⇒ **h = 3.5 cm**.

Perimeter of the rectangle = 2(l + b) = 2(h + r) = 2(3.5 + 21) = 49 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Volume (V) = 4851 cm³, Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 462 cm².

**Formula Used:** Volume = πr²h; CSA = 2πrh; Perimeter of rectangle = 2(length + breadth).

⇒ Dividing V by CSA: (πr²h) / (2πrh) = 4851 / 462

⇒ r / 2 = 10.5

⇒ **r = 21 cm**

⇒ Putting r in CSA: 2 × (22/7) × 21 × h = 462

⇒ 132 × h = 462

⇒ **h = 3.5 cm**

⇒ When a rectangle is rotated about its **length**, height of cylinder (h) = length (l) and radius (r) = breadth (b).

⇒ Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 2(3.5 + 21) = 2 × 24.5 = 49 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rotation of Rectangle

If a rectangle is rotated about its **length** (l), then l becomes the **height** (h) and the **breadth** (b) becomes the **radius** (r).

Cylinder Formulas

Total Surface Area = 2πr(h + r). The ratio of Volume to CSA is always r/2.

Perimeter of Rectangle

The distance around the outside of a rectangle, calculated as 2 × (length + width).</p

**Calculations:**

⇒ 14 ÷ 7 = 12 ÷ y

questions.question: Which of the following is the greatest number that divides 137 and 198 and leaves 7 and 3 as respective remainders?

Subtract the **remainders** from the given numbers: (137 − 7) = 130 and (198 − 3) = 195.

Factors of 130 = 65 × 2; Factors of 195 = 65 × 3.

The **highest common factor** is 65.

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

Also known as **GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)**, it is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder.

To find the **greatest number** that divides a, b, c leaving remainders x, y, z, find HCF of (a−x), (b−y), and (c−z).

States that for any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.</p

questions.question: The ratio of three numbers is 10: 15:13. If 10 percent of the first number is 66, what would be 50 percent of the difference of the third and second number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the numbers be **10x**, **15x**, and **13x**.

Given: 10% of 10x = 66 ⇒ 1x = 66.

Required value: 50% of (15x − 13x) = 50% of 2x = 1x.

Since 1x = 66, the required value is 66.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60e7fc45d8de0a7085cb9cdc487df76879800f2c5434048f0307b2dc868ed789.png] 

**Given:** Ratio = 10 : 15 : 13 | 10% of 1st number = 66

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 10x, 15x, and 13x.

⇒ 10% of 10x = (10/100) × 10x = 1x

⇒ x = 66

⇒ Difference between 2nd and 3rd number = 15x − 13x = 2x

⇒ 50% of the difference = (50/100) × 2x = 1x

⇒ Since x = 66, the value is 66.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

If a : b : c is the ratio, then the numbers can be expressed as ax, bx, and cx where x is a common multiplier.

Percentage Calculation

To find p% of a number N, use the formula (p/100) × N. Note that 50% is equivalent to half (1/2) of the value.

Base Value Logic

When the percentage and the ratio part result in 1 unit of 'x', that value directly represents the scaling factor for all other calculations.</p

questions.question: Financial inclusion has been a major goal of post-1991 economic reforms in India. Which of the following flagship schemes was launched in 2014 to promote financial inclusion through universal access to banking facilities?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on **28th August 2014** to promote financial inclusion in India.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **universal access to banking services**, including savings accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• Under PMJDY, individuals can open a **zero-balance savings account** with access to a RuPay debit card and accidental insurance cover.
 
• The scheme is an integral part of India's financial inclusion strategy and has resulted in the opening of millions of bank accounts, particularly in rural areas.
 
• PMJDY includes additional benefits such as **overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000** for account holders and direct benefit transfer (DBT) integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion**

 
 
• It refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and adequate credit at affordable costs for all individuals, especially the marginalized and low-income groups.
 
• Financial inclusion helps reduce poverty by enabling people to save, borrow, and invest.
 
 
 
• **RuPay Debit Card**
 
 
• RuPay is India's indigenous payment network developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
• PMJDY account holders are provided with RuPay debit cards that offer accidental insurance cover.
 
 
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**
 
 
• DBT ensures that subsidies and benefits are directly transferred to the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
 
• This reduces leakages and ensures transparency in government schemes.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PMJDY**
 
 
• As of 2023, PMJDY has helped open over 48 crore bank accounts, with a significant proportion in rural areas.
 
• The scheme has facilitated access to formal banking services for millions of previously unbanked individuals.

questions.question: A group of people consists of men, women and children. Among them, 20% are men, 30% are women and the rest are children, and their average weights are 50 kg, 40 kg and 30 kg, respectively. The average weight of the group (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Men** : **Women** : **Children** = 20% : 30% : 50% = 2 : 3 : 5

Multiply the ratio units by their respective **average weights**:

Sum = (2 × 50) + (3 × 40) + (5 × 30) = 100 + 120 + 150 = 370

Average of the **group** = Total Sum ÷ Total Ratio units = 370 ÷ 10 = 37 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of **Men** = 20% | **Average weight** = 50 kg

Percentage of **Women** = 30% | **Average weight** = 40 kg

Percentage of **Children** = 100% − (20% + 30%) = 50% | **Average weight** = 30 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65196577007739c1d99a0d661b5bbe20b9006bfbab086e1f8878339ee538632a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂ + n₃ × x₃) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + n₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of people in the **group** be 100.

⇒ Number of **Men** = 20, **Women** = 30, **Children** = 50.

⇒ Total weight of Men = 20 × 50 = 1000 kg.

⇒ Total weight of Women = 30 × 40 = 1200 kg.

⇒ Total weight of Children = 50 × 30 = 1500 kg.

⇒ Total weight of the group = 1000 + 1200 + 1500 = 3700 kg.

⇒ Average weight of the group = 3700 ÷ 100 = 37 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is used when components of a group have different weights or frequencies. Formula: Aₐvg = (Σnᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σnᵢ.

Deviation Method

Assume a mean (e.g., 40) and calculate the net deviation: 20%(+10) + 30%(0) + 50%(−10). Net = +2 − 5 = −3. Final Avg = 40 − 3 = 37 kg.

Ratio Property of Averages

The average of a group remains unchanged if the number of members in each sub-group is scaled by the same ratio constant.</p

questions.question: In MS Word, when a user wants to move a block of text from one part of a document to another, which of the following sequences of actions should be performed?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Cut" and "Paste" functions in MS Word allow users to efficiently move text or objects from one part of a document to another.
 
• When text is "Cut," it is removed from its original location and stored temporarily in the clipboard until "Paste" is executed.
 
• This method ensures that the original text does not remain duplicated in the document, unlike the "Copy" function.
 
• Users can move the cursor to the desired location before pasting the text, ensuring precise placement.

• The clipboard content can be pasted multiple times unless overwritten by a new "Cut" or "Copy" action.
 
 
 
• **Difference between Cut and Copy:**
 
 
• "Cut" removes the selected content from its original location, while "Copy" leaves the content intact.
 
• Both operations store the selected content in the clipboard for future use.

questions.question: If the selling price of a bed is 2-times of initial, then the profit is 8-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage (in %).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** be x and **Cost Price (CP)** be c.

Initial **Profit (P₁)** = x − c.

New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = 2x and New **Profit (P₂)** = 8 × (x − c).

Since P₂ = SP₂ − CP, we have 8(x − c) = 2x − c.

8x − 8c = 2x − c ⇒ 6x = 7c ⇒ x/c = 7/6.

Initial Profit% = (x − c)/c × 100 = (7 − 6)/6 × 100 = 100/6 = 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** New SP = 2 × Old SP; New Profit = 8 × Old Profit.
**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd6dce648ad67ad950cef4b3f6ce0ce17e1d36071ff1eaf3b53c281510ebd6d3.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price** = C and initial **Selling Price** = S.
⇒ Initial **Profit** (P) = S − C.
⇒ According to the question: 8 × (S − C) = 2S − C.
⇒ 8S − 8C = 2S − C ⇒ 6S = 7C.
⇒ S = (7/6)C.
⇒ Initial Profit = (7/6)C − C = (1/6)C.
⇒ Initial **Profit Percentage** = ((1/6)C ÷ C) × 100 = 100/6 = 16.666...% ≈ 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Fundamentals

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Profit = SP − CP. Profit% is always calculated on the CP unless stated otherwise.

Effect of SP change on Profit

If CP remains constant, the increase in Profit is exactly equal to the increase in Selling Price.</p

questions.question: At STP, the number of molecules present in 5.6 L of O2 gas is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.5055 x 10²³**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• At standard temperature and pressure (STP), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies a volume of **22.4 L**.
 
• The number of molecules in 1 mole of a substance is given by **Avogadro's number = 6.022 x 10²³**.
 
• Given volume = 5.6 L, which corresponds to **5.6 ÷ 22.4 = 0.25 moles**.
 
• The number of molecules in 0.25 moles can be calculated as **0.25 x 6.022 x 10²³ = 1.5055 x 10²³**.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **1.05055 x 10²³**, i.e., Option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP):**

 
 
• STP refers to conditions where the temperature is 0°C (273.15 K) and the pressure is 1 atmosphere (101.325 kPa).
 
• Under these conditions, 1 mole of an ideal gas occupies a volume of 22.4 L.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• It is the number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in 1 mole of a substance.
 
• The value of Avogadro's number is approximately **6.022 x 10²³**.
 
 
 
• **Mole Concept:**
 
 
• A mole is a fundamental unit in chemistry representing the quantity of substance.
 
• It is used to relate the mass of a substance to the number of particles it contains.
 
 
 
• **Ideal Gas Law:**
 
 
• The ideal gas law is expressed as PV = nRT, where P = pressure, V = volume, n = moles, R = gas constant, and T = temperature.
 
• Under STP conditions, the molar volume of an ideal gas is fixed at 22.4 L.

questions.question: If at the same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest, compounded annually, is 41, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Difference (D)** between **CI** and **SI** for 2 years = 41 − 40 = ₹1

**SI** for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

**Rate (R)** = (Difference ÷ SI of 1 year) × 100 = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5%

**Principal (P)** = (SI of 1 year × 100) ÷ R = (20 × 100) ÷ 5 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Simple Interest (SI)** for 2 years = ₹40

Total **Compound Interest (CI)** for 2 years = ₹41

Time (T) = 2 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51039f7f9411d69e50fb27695726aad330858cf5b4479725f71633160c833dc9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1st year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ In **Compound Interest**, the interest for the 1st year is the same as **SI** = ₹20

⇒ **CI** for the 2ⁿd year = Total **CI** − 1st year interest = 41 − 20 = ₹21

⇒ The extra ₹1 (21 − 20) is the interest earned on the 1st year interest (₹20)

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5% per annum

⇒ Now, using **SI** formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = (P × 5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = (P × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ 40 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 40 × 10 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference (D) is given by the formula D = P(R ÷ 100)².

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 Years

The relationship is expressed as CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200.

Effective Rate for Compound Interest

For a rate R% for 2 years, the effective CI rate is R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Privatisation can be partial, involving minority shareholding by the private sector. What is the government's shareholding threshold in a PSU for it to be considered privatised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than 51%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) is considered privatised when the government’s shareholding falls **below 51%.**
 
• This threshold ensures that the private sector holds a majority share, providing control and decision-making power.
 
• Privatisation can be partial or complete, depending on the percentage of shares divested by the government.
 
• Privatisation aims to improve efficiency, promote competition, and reduce the financial burden of PSUs on the government.
 
• Examples of privatised PSUs include Air India and Bharat Aluminium Company Limited (BALCO).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation**

 
 
• It refers to the transfer of ownership, management, or control of a government-owned enterprise to the private sector.
 
• It can occur through mechanisms like disinvestment, public-private partnerships, or outright sale of assets.
 
• Privatisation is often undertaken to enhance efficiency and reduce government expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment**
 
 
• Disinvestment involves the sale or liquidation of government-owned shares in PSUs.
 
• It is aimed at raising revenue and encouraging private sector participation.
 
• Major disinvestment initiatives include Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and IDBI Bank.
 
 
 
• **Types of Privatisation**
 
 
• **Partial Privatisation:** Government retains a minority shareholding (more than 49%) while transferring control to the private sector.
 
• **Complete Privatisation:** Government sells 100% of its stake to the private sector, relinquishing all ownership rights.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Privatisation**
 
 
• Improves operational efficiency due to private sector expertise.
 
• Promotes competition and innovation in industries.
 
• Reduces fiscal burden on the government.
 
• Enhances service quality for consumers.

questions.question: Chemical fertilisers were used intensively during the Green Revolution. What was the result of their overuse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil salinity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Intensive use of chemical fertilizers** during the Green Revolution led to an increase in soil salinity, negatively impacting agricultural productivity.
 
• High levels of fertilizers, especially nitrogen-based ones, can disrupt soil chemistry, reducing its ability to retain water and nutrients.
 
• **Soil salinity affects crop growth** by restricting the plants' ability to absorb water and essential nutrients due to osmotic stress.
 
• Regions practicing intensive farming with chemical inputs, such as Punjab and Haryana, reported significant degradation of soil health due to salinity.
 
• Efforts to mitigate soil salinity include techniques like organic farming, crop rotation, and the use of bio-fertilizers to restore soil health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil Salinity:**

 
 
• It refers to the accumulation of soluble salts in the soil, which can harm plant growth and soil health.
 
• Saline soils are often characterized by white crusts and reduced agricultural yield.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• A period during the 1960s-70s marked by increased agricultural production due to modern techniques, including high-yield crop varieties and chemical fertilizers.
 
• While it solved food shortages, it had environmental consequences such as soil degradation and water table depletion.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Chemical Fertilizers:**

questions.question: Kalpana and Sudha got 656 and 697 marks, respectively, in the same examination. If Kalpana scored 32% marks, then what is the percentage of marks scored by Sudha?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Percentage** is directly proportional to the **marks** obtained.

Marks 656 corresponds to 32%.

1 mark corresponds to 32 ÷ 656%.

697 marks correspond to (32 ÷ 656) × 697% = (1 ÷ 20.5) × 697% = 34%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Marks of **Kalpana** = 656

Percentage of **Kalpana** = 32%

Marks of **Sudha** = 697

**Formula Used:**

Total Marks = (Obtained Marks × 100) ÷ Percentage

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/575b51d152d68b46933dbe8cd4d015023a3280d1ef7ce60db532361a706a98a6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Total Marks** be T.

⇒ 32% of T = 656

⇒ (32 ÷ 100) × T = 656

⇒ T = (656 × 100) ÷ 32

⇒ T = 20.5 × 100 = 2050

⇒ **Sudha's Percentage** = (Sudha's Marks ÷ T) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (697 ÷ 2050) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 6970 ÷ 205 = 34%

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. Useful for comparing growth or reduction.

Base Change Property

If the total marks are constant, marks obtained are directly proportional to the percentage: M₁/P₁ = M₂/P₂.

Conversion of Fraction to Percentage

To convert any fraction x/y into percentage, multiply it by 100 and add the % symbol.</p

⇒ **(a + b)²** = 50²

questions.question: The average of first 17 multiples of 13 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **average** of the first **n multiples** of a number **x** is given by the formula: **x × (n + 1) ÷ 2**.

In this question, **x = 13** and **n = 17**.

⇒ Average = 13 × (17 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 13 × 18 ÷ 2 = 13 × 9 = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = 17

Multiplier = 13

The sequence is: 13, 26, 39, ..., (13 × 17)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f46658c9b1c1fee060695905f122f6f35ff9d7e21e9e08e2632aab38cf66599.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the **Average** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ First term (a) = 13 × 1 = 13

⇒ Last term (l) = 13 × 17 = 221

⇒ Average = (13 + 221) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 234 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of AP

In any series with a common difference, the **average** is always the **middle term** if the number of terms is odd, calculated as (n + 1)/2 th term.

Sum of AP

The sum of an AP is Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d] or Sₙ = n/2 × [first term + last term].

Average of first n Natural Numbers

The average of the first **n** natural numbers is (n + 1) ÷ 2. For multiples of **k**, just multiply this average by **k**.</p

questions.question: An article's cost price is ₹300, and the marked price is mentioned as ₹1,032. What is the profit percentage of the seller if he sells it by allowing a discount of 50% on the marked price?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** can be found directly.

MP = ₹1,032 and Discount = 50%.

SP = 50% of MP = 1,032 ÷ 2 = ₹516.

Profit = SP − CP = 516 − 300 = ₹216.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (216 ÷ 300) × 100 = 72%.

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

⇒ First, calculate **Selling Price (SP)** = 1,032 × (100 − 50) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1,032 × 50 ÷ 100 = 516

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 516 − 300 = 216

⇒ Profit Percentage = (216 ÷ 300) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 72%

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the MP to reach the Selling Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Profit/Loss on Cost Price

Unless otherwise stated, **Profit** or **Loss percentage** is always calculated based on the **Cost Price (CP)**.

questions.question: Let a be an odd positive integer. If the roots of a quadratic equation x² - (a - 1)x + 4a + 7 = 0 are integers, then the least value of a is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the quadratic equation x² − (a − 1)x + 4a + 7 = 0, use the relation between roots α and β.

Using **Simon's Favorite Factoring Trick**: (α − 4)(β − 4) = 4 + 7 + 16 = 27.

Possible **integer factors** of 27 are (1, 27) and (3, 9).

Case (3, 9): α − 4 = 3 ⇒ α = 7 and β − 4 = 9 ⇒ β = 13.

Then, a − 1 = α + β ⇒ a − 1 = 20 ⇒ a = 21.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Quadratic equation x² − (a − 1)x + 4a + 7 = 0 where **a** is an **odd positive integer** and roots are **integers**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of roots (α + β) = −b/a and Product of roots (αβ) = c/a.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5710cf517c0359c4e7a15a254409da54dc06fbcfe7f64aa36ad6be0b6d7ad04c.png] 

⇒ α + β = a − 1

⇒ αβ = 4a + 7

⇒ From the first equation, a = α + β + 1. Substitute this into the second equation:

⇒ αβ = 4(α + β + 1) + 7

⇒ αβ − 4α − 4β = 4 + 7

⇒ αβ − 4α − 4β + 16 = 11 + 16

⇒ (α − 4)(β − 4) = 27

⇒ Factor pairs of 27 are (1, 27), (3, 9), (−1, −27), (−3, −9).

⇒ For (1, 27): α = 5, β = 31 ⇒ a = 5 + 31 + 1 = 37.

⇒ For (3, 9): α = 7, β = 13 ⇒ a = 7 + 13 + 1 = 21.

⇒ Negative pairs result in negative values for a (e.g., −19, −3), which are not positive integers.

⇒ Comparing 37 and 21, the least value is 21.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Integer Roots Condition

For a quadratic equation with integer coefficients to have integer roots, the **Discriminant (D = b² − 4ac)** must be a perfect square.

Vieta's Formulas

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Simon's Favorite Factoring Trick

The expression xy + kx + my can be factored as (x + m)(y + k) − km. This is highly useful in solving equations with integer constraints.</p

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 18 days. If A alone can do it in 24 days, then B alone can do one-fourth of the same work in_______ days.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **B** = 1/18 − 1/24 = (4 − 3)/72 = 1/72

Time for **B** to do **Full Work** = 72 days

Time for **B** to do **1/4th Work** = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **(A + B)** = 18 days, Time taken by **A** = 24 days.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time; Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 A + B 18 72 4 
 A 24 3 

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of **(A + B)** − Efficiency of **A**

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/day

⇒ **One-fourth** of Total Work = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 units

⇒ Time taken by **B** for 1/4th work = 18 ÷ 1 = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Formula

If two people work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂.

Work and Time Relation

Time is **inversely proportional** to efficiency for a constant amount of work. Work = Time × Efficiency.</p

questions.question: In January 2025, India mourned the loss of Dr K.S. Manilal, a pioneering scientist in which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Botany**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. K.S. Manilal was an eminent Indian botanist renowned for his contributions to taxonomy, plant sciences, and history of botany.
 
• He specialized in the study of the flora of India, particularly focusing on the Western Ghats and Kerala region.
 
• Dr. Manilal is celebrated for his translation and commentary on the 17th-century work "Hortus Malabaricus," a comprehensive treatise on the medicinal plants of Malabar.
 
• His efforts in preserving and interpreting historical botanical manuscripts have contributed significantly to the understanding of India's biodiversity.
 
• Dr. Manilal has received numerous accolades for his pioneering work in botany, including national and international recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taxonomy:**

 
 
• Taxonomy is the science of classifying organisms based on their characteristics, origin, and evolutionary relationships.
 
• It plays a crucial role in understanding biodiversity and conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Hortus Malabaricus:**
 
 
• A landmark 17th-century botanical text documenting the medicinal plants of Malabar (modern-day Kerala).
 
• It was originally authored by Hendrik van Rheede and involved contributions from local physicians and botanists.
 
• Dr. Manilal's translation and commentary made this work accessible to a global audience.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• Home to a wide variety of endemic flora and fauna, making it a focus area for botanical research.
 
 
 
• **Medicinal Botany:**
 
 
• The study of plants with therapeutic properties and their application in traditional and modern medicine.
 
• India has a rich heritage of medicinal botany, with Ayurveda being a prominent traditional system of healthcare.
